title: FLUENcy-targeted cognitive Training after subthalamic Deep Brain Stimulation in Parkinson's Disease
summary:
People with Parkinson’s disease may experience changes in certain thinking abilities after deep brain stimulation, in addition to changes in their movement symptoms. One ability that may be particularly affected is finding the right words quickly. Such changes can influence communication, everyday activities, and quality of life. However, targeted training of thinking abilities is not currently part of routine care following deep brain stimulation.

This study examines how thinking abilities change after deep brain stimulation in connection with a digital training program. Three months after surgery, participants will be randomly assigned to either a training group or a wait-list control group. The training group will complete a digital cognitive training two to three times per week for three months, targeting different thinking abilities. During this period, the control group will initially receive no additional training.

Before and after the training period, participants’ thinking abilities, their own perception of their cognitive functioning, quality of life, and other symptoms will be assessed. A further assessment twelve months after surgery will examine how these outcomes develop over a longer period. After this assessment, participants in the wait-list control group will also receive access to the digital training program. In addition, brain scans will be used to explore whether certain characteristics are associated with individual changes observed during the study. The study aims to improve our understanding of how thinking abilities develop after deep brain stimulation.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Confirmed diagnosis of Parkinson’s disease based on routine clinical practice and in accordance with the diagnostic criteria of the Movement Disorder Society (MDS)
- 3 months post-surgery following bilateral STN-DBS
- Cognitive vulnerability, defined as the presence of at least one of the following criteria (3 months post-surgery):
1. Mild cognitive impairment based on a global cognitive screening test (MoCA < 26)
2. Subjectively reported cognitive decline, assessed via MDS-UPDRS Item 1.1 (score ≥ 1)
3. Reduced verbal fluency, defined as an RWT z-score ≤ 1 on at least one RWT subtest
- Normal or adequately corrected vision and hearing
- German as a native language or sufficient proficiency in German to complete the test procedures
- Sufficient computer skills and access to a personal desktop computer or laptop with an internet connection
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe neurological or psychiatric comorbidities or life-threatening medical conditions
- Impaired or absent capacity to provide written informed consent prior to study enrollment
- Current prescription for cognitive training (analog or digital) or personal use of NeuroNation or comparable cognitive training applications within the last 12 months
